/**
 * Maps one Recently Viewed product onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
 *
 * **Input source revised 2026-09-08 (build plan §2, "Interim data source") — Einstein is "Not
 * Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site, so this build shipped against a browser-tracked
 * view-history stand-in instead.** Input was, for that interim period, a plain Commerce API
 * `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`), exactly as returned by
 * the interim build's own dedicated fetch utility's `getProducts` call (`expand: [
 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`, `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`) —
 * the same underlying Shopper Products shape the original Einstein-sourced design used, minus the
 * Einstein-specific `rec`/flat-`image` wrapper fields `fetchRecProductDetails`
 * (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) used to bolt on. This
 * mapper's own output contract and scope (image-only, no gallery, no was/now pricing — A2's
 * `recentlyViewed` variation decision, unchanged) were unaffected; only the shape of what it read
 * on the way in changed, and with it, `selectPrimaryImage`'s fallback below: there was no longer a
 * separate flat Einstein image to fall back to, so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no
 * usable `src`" and "there is no usable image at all" were the same case.
 *
 * **Superseded 2026-09-15 (build plan step E1, formalised by step E4): input is once again the
 * Einstein rec, not a plain Commerce API product.** The interim fetch utility and its companion
 * history-tracking hook referenced above are deleted as of build plan step E4 (see
 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own module docblock for the full "why"). Einstein's own
 * `fetchRecProductDetails` (`use-einstein.js:465-520`) already merges each rec with its full
 * hydrated `getProducts` record before this mapper ever sees it (`{...rec, ...product, productId,
 * image}`) — a strict superset of the plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` shape this mapper read
 * during the interim period described above, so nothing below needed a functional change; this
 * note is the only edit build plan step E4 made to this file.
 *
 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used directly (AGENTS.md > Type
 * Definitions) — with the Einstein-specific input shape gone, there is no longer any hand-rolled
 * field on the input type at all.
 *
 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price), not was/now sale-price detection
 * (`originalPrice`) — but that is a scope choice, not a data limitation. **Correction
 * (2026-09-08, pre-dates and is unaffected by the input-source revision above):** an earlier
 * version of this comment claimed the merged Einstein shape "has no equivalent of"
 * `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic — verified inaccurate, and equally true of the plain
 * `getProducts` shape this mapper read during the interim period: that now-removed fetch utility
 * already requested `perPricebook: true`, so `product.tieredPrices` was present, and base SFCC's `getPriceData`
 * (`app/utils/product-utils.js`) already derives `listPrice`/`isOnSale` from exactly that field —
 * nothing is missing, it's simply not called here. The real reason `originalPrice` isn't mapped is
 * that the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`), so
 * there is nothing for it to feed. Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future
 * consumer of this same mapper (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this
 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.
 */
import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
import { sortImagesBySequence, resolveFallbackColour, resolveRequiredAlt } from './productCardMappingHelpers';

/**
 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
 * — not hand-rolled). A plain alias, not an augmentation: the Einstein rec this mapper reads again
 * as of build plan step E1/E4 needs nothing bolted on either — `Product.id` is used directly, and
 * there is no separate flat-image field to reconcile. Kept as a
 * named alias (rather than importing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` directly at each call site)
 * so this module's own input type has a name that documents its role here.
 */
export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;

/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;

/**
 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
 * for why.
 */
export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
>;

/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';

/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';

/** The one shape this mapper sorts — whatever `ImageGroup.images` actually holds. */
type ImageGroupImage = NonNullable<ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup['images']>[number];

/**
 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`, which silently showed the on-model
 * shot (image `2`) as primary instead of the flat-lay shot (always image `1`).
 *
 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — see
 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10). This file's own images are the raw SDK shape (`disBaseLink`/`link`,
 * not a flat `src`), hence the explicit accessor.
 */
const sortByImageSequence = (images: ImageGroupImage[]): ImageGroupImage[] =>
  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.disBaseLink || image.link || '');

/**
 * Resolves which real colour this product's one image should come from — now the shared
 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, since there is no
 * `representedProduct` branch to add here: this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
 * (from `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback.
 * Returns `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectPrimaryImage` below then falls
 * back to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
 */
const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct): string | undefined =>
  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);

/**
 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
 * `images` at all).
 *
 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
 * **colour-scoped first, then viewtype-only as a fallback** — same two-pass fix, same reasoning,
 * as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectColourScopedImages`, closing a real bug confirmed
 * live on `4673TS251`: with no colour scoping at all, an older, untagged, genuinely-404 medium
 * group and a newer, correctly colour-tagged one are both candidates, and the untagged one wins by
 * default purely because it happens to sit first in the API's own array order. Scoping by colour
 * excludes the untagged group outright. The fallback pass exists for the opposite real case — a
 * genuinely single-colour product whose one medium group carries no `variationAttributes` tag at
 * all (nothing to disambiguate) — which a strict colour-scoped lookup alone would exclude and
 * return nothing for. Never the reverse: a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
 * avoid re-mixing colours.
 *
 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
 *
 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
 *   be empty on.
 */
const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
  const colour = resolveViewedColour(product);

  const colourScopedGroups = colour
    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
    : [];

  const groups =
    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
      ? colourScopedGroups
      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);

  const [groupImage] = sortByImageSequence(groups[0]?.images ?? []);
  if (!groupImage) return null;

  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
  if (!src) return null;

  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
  // decorative alt: '' convention) — shared resolveRequiredAlt (productCardMappingHelpers.ts).
  const alt = resolveRequiredAlt(groupImage.alt, productName);
  return { src, alt };
};

/**
 * @param product - A Commerce-API-product-shaped value — as of build plan step E1/E4, the Einstein
 *   recommendation object `fetchRecProductDetails` returns (a strict superset of the plain
 *   `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` this mapper is typed against) — or `undefined`/`null` while
 *   that data is not yet available.
 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
 * @param buildUrl - Site/locale prefixer, normally `useMultiSite()`'s own `buildUrl`. Fixed
 *   2026-09-15 (CodeRabbit finding, confirmed): `productUrlBuilder` alone only ever returns a bare
 *   `/product/:id` path with no site/locale awareness, and `ZimmProductCard`'s `recentlyViewed`
 *   render branch links via a plain `react-router-dom` `Link` (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
 *   `MediaOnlyCardLink`), not the base SFCC `Link` that would otherwise apply this prefix
 *   internally — so a shopper on a non-default site/locale previously always landed on the
 *   default site/locale instead of the storefront they were actually browsing. Same fix, same
 *   reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectProductListCard`
 *   (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:273,290`) — injected as a
 *   parameter for the same reason `formatPrice` already is: this stays a pure function with no
 *   hook dependency of its own.
 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product
 *   has no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
 */
export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
  buildUrl: (path: string) => string,
): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
  if (!product?.name) return null;

  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
  if (!primaryImage) return null;

  return {
    id: product.id,
    href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id })),
    name: product.name,
    primaryImage,
    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
    currentPrice:
      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
  };
};

1	import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

11	// Zimmermann's own constant — NOT the base package above (see recommended-products/index.tsx's
12	// own comment on this exact gotcha: a named import off the base package's untyped module compiles
13	// but is undefined at runtime). APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — this page has no
14	// PageContainer/layerStyle second containment layer for PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX to correctly
15	// cancel; see that constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the bug this distinction
16	// fixes (a real, live-confirmed horizontal overflow, Marcel, 2026-09-10).
17	import { APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX } from 'app/constants';
18	import { ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid';
19	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
20	import {
21	  selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard,
22	  resolveOrderableVariant,
23	} from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
24	import type {
25	  RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard,
26	  RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
27	} from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
28	
29	// Message-id namespace follows this codebase's existing `<page>.<category>.<key>` convention
30	// (see home.*, product_list.*, product_detail.* in their own index.tsx files) -- `recently_viewed`
31	// is this page's own snake_case prefix.
32	const messages = defineMessages({
33	  title: {
34	    id: 'recently_viewed.heading.title',
35	    defaultMessage: 'Recently Viewed',
36	  },
37	  // Real ICU `plural` selector, not string interpolation -- decided explicitly this session
38	  // (build plan §B1, "go for it" -- Marcel, 2026-09-08). `#` is replaced by the matched `count`
39	  // value at each branch, so this renders "1 item" / "16 items" correctly with no separate
40	  // singular-check needed at the call site. Lowercase "item(s)" -- corrected 2026-09-11 (Marcel).
41	  itemCount: {
42	    id: 'recently_viewed.label.item_count',
43	    defaultMessage: '{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}',
44	  },
45	  emptyHeading: {
46	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.heading',
47	    defaultMessage: "You haven't viewed anything yet.",
48	  },
49	  emptyBodyRegistered: {
50	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_registered',
51	    defaultMessage: 'Continue shopping to start building your history.',
52	  },
53	  emptyBodyGuest: {
54	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_guest',
55	    defaultMessage: 'Sign in to keep track of your history, or continue shopping.',
56	  },
57	  continueShopping: {
58	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.continue_shopping',
59	    defaultMessage: 'Continue Shopping',
60	  },
61	  signIn: {
62	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.sign_in',
63	    defaultMessage: 'Sign In',
64	  },
65	  // Same copy, same event, as product-list/index.tsx's own `product_list.toast.added_to_bag` --
66	  // a distinct message id under this page's own `recently_viewed.*` namespace (see this file's own
67	  // message-id-namespace comment above) rather than importing that page's message across a page
68	  // boundary.
69	  addedToBag: {
70	    id: 'recently_viewed.toast.added_to_bag',
71	    defaultMessage: 'Added to bag',
72	  },
73	});
74	
75	// Plain literal, not run through react-intl -- matches home/index.tsx's own un-translated Seo
76	// `description` precedent (`description="Commerce Cloud Retail React App"`). The build plan's
77	// SEO section only calls out `title` for useIntl; this page's own description copy was never
78	// specified, so it is authored here rather than invented as a translated message with no source.
79	const PAGE_DESCRIPTION = "Browse the products you've recently viewed at Zimmermann.";
80	
81	type EmptyRecentlyViewedProps = {
82	  isRegistered: boolean;
83	};
84	
85	/**
86	 * SFCC-84's own empty-state design (build plan §B2 "Empty state"). There is no AC or Figma design
87	 * for this state at all; copy and structure are ported from the real `EmptyCart` precedent
88	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`), per
89	 * Marcel's own direction ("look for a pattern in the existing codebase and build off that"): a
90	 * `Box` > `Center` > `Stack` layout, an `isRegistered`-branched body message, and a
91	 * `Button as={Link}` CTA pattern (the base SFCC `Link`, not a raw `react-router-dom` one, so the
92	 * "Continue Shopping"/"Sign In" hrefs get this storefront's real multi-site URL prefixing --
93	 * `use-multi-site.js`'s `buildUrl`, called internally by that `Link` -- the same reason `EmptyCart`
94	 * itself uses it).
95	 *
96	 * **Deliberately not a byte-for-byte styling port.** `EmptyCart`'s own prop values
97	 * (`fontSize={['18px', '2xl']}`, `color="gray.700"`, `color="blue.600"`,
98	 * `width={['343px', '220px']}`) are raw base-Chakra literals with no relationship to Zimmermann's
99	 * design tokens, and this codebase's styling hierarchy
100	 * (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`) requires `textStyle`/`var(--zimm-*)` for new
101	 * Zimmermann-authored UI and forbids a raw px/rem literal outright. With no confirmed empty-state
102	 * Figma spec to derive exact values from, this uses the nearest reasonable *registered* tokens
103	 * (`heading2`/`body1` text styles, `text-default`/`text-secondary` colours, `2xl`/`2xs`/`m`
104	 * spacing) instead -- an autonomous styling judgement call (see this module's own bottom-of-file
105	 * decision log), not a design decision that conflicts with an existing one (there is no existing
106	 * design here to conflict with).
107	 *
108	 * **No icon.** `EmptyCart` renders `BasketIcon` above its heading and `AccountIcon` on its
109	 * "Sign In" button. Checked directly against `overrides/app/components/icons`' full export list:
110	 * no Recently-Viewed-thematic icon exists (no eye/clock/history glyph), and forcing an unrelated
111	 * one -- `BasketIcon` itself, or reusing `AccountIcon` -- would misrepresent this page rather than
112	 * help it, so both are omitted; heading + copy + CTA(s) alone still satisfies the established
113	 * empty-state pattern this page is following.
114	 *
115	 * `useIntl` is called directly in this leaf, not passed down as a prop -- this is the
116	 * Context-backed, app-wide exception `.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition documents for
117	 * `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` specifically (this is a private, single-parent sub-component of this page,
118	 * not a component exported from its own folder, so it needs no story/test of its own either --
119	 * its behaviour is exercised through this page's own `index.test.tsx`).
120	 */
121	const EmptyRecentlyViewed = ({ isRegistered }: EmptyRecentlyViewedProps) => {
122	  const intl = useIntl();
123	
124	  return (
125	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-empty">
126	      <Center>
127	        <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xl)" textAlign="center" paddingY="var(--zimm-scale-4xl)">
128	          <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xs)">
129	            <Text textStyle="heading2" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
130	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyHeading)}
131	            </Text>
132	            <Text textStyle="body1" color="var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)">
133	              {isRegistered
134	                ? intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyRegistered)
135	                : intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyGuest)}
136	            </Text>
137	          </Stack>
138	          <Stack direction={{ base: 'column', sm: 'row' }} justify="center" spacing="var(--zimm-scale-m)">
139	            {/* Continue Shopping is the loud/primary CTA for a registered shopper (their only
140	                CTA), but yields primary emphasis to Sign In for a guest -- same isRegistered-driven
141	                emphasis flip EmptyCart's own solid/outline split encodes, re-expressed here via
142	                ZimmButton's own primary/secondary variants instead of a raw colour override. */}
143	            <Button
144	              as={Link}
145	              href="/"
146	              variant={isRegistered ? 'primary' : 'secondary'}
147	              width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}
148	            >
149	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.continueShopping)}
150	            </Button>
151	            {!isRegistered && (
152	              <Button as={Link} href="/account" variant="primary" width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}>
153	                {intl.formatMessage(messages.signIn)}
154	              </Button>
155	            )}
156	          </Stack>
157	        </Stack>
158	      </Center>
159	    </Box>
160	  );
161	};
162	
163	/**
164	 * SFCC-84 -- Recently Viewed Full History page container (build plan §B2, rewired to real Einstein
165	 * data by build plan step E2). Thin container: calls `useEinstein()` directly, fires
166	 * `getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)` once on mount, reads
167	 * `recommendations.recs` off that same hook once the request resolves, maps each rec through
168	 * `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (filtering the hard `null` gate every mapper in this
169	 * codebase uses), and renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` -- or, with no recs, this page's own empty
170	 * state (`EmptyRecentlyViewed` above). Matches `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own
171	 * Recently-Viewed branch exactly (build plan step E1, already committed) -- same
172	 * `useEinstein()`/`getRecommendations`/`recommendations.recs` chain, same mapper family, just this
173	 * page's own container instead of that shared rail.
174	 *
175	 * **`useMultiSite()`'s own `buildUrl` is now also called here (2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding,
176	 * confirmed) and threaded into `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`** — matching
177	 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own identical fix for `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. Before this,
178	 * every card's `href` was `productUrlBuilder`'s bare, unprefixed `/product/:id` path, so a shopper
179	 * on a non-default site/locale who clicked a card on this page landed on the default site/locale
180	 * instead of the storefront they were actually browsing. See that mapper's own docblock for the
181	 * full reasoning and the established precedent it follows
182	 * (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:273,290`).
183	 *
184	 * **Replaces the interim, browser-tracked view-history hook and its companion product-fetch
185	 * utility this page previously shipped with** (removed in build plan step E4 -- this page no
186	 * longer references either one, and the files themselves are now gone too; see
187	 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own module docblock, which named them directly, for the full
188	 * "why" of that interim build and why it was superseded). `recommendations.recs` is a strict
189	 * superset of the plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` shape the interim build fed this same
190	 * mapper (Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`, `use-einstein.js:465-520`, already merges each
191	 * rec with its full hydrated `getProducts` record before this component ever sees it), so
192	 * `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` needed no change at all -- confirmed directly against that
193	 * function's body, not assumed.
194	 *
195	 * **Known, already-flagged gap, not introduced here:** `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`'s
196	 * `badge` field is always `undefined` -- the plain `getProducts` endpoint this build reads from has
197	 * no confirmed `c_productBadges` field (see that mapper's own docblock's "Badge" section). A card
198	 * rendered by this page will never show a badge yet; this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap for
199	 * this step, not a bug in this file.
200	 *
201	 * **Empty-state gate (build plan step E2, decision #3; corrected 2026-09-15 -- CodeRabbit finding,
202	 * personally verified before treating as valid):** `cards.length > 0` renders the grid;
203	 * `!isLoading && cards.length === 0` renders `EmptyRecentlyViewed`; anything else (i.e. `isLoading`
204	 * still `true`, request in flight) renders neither -- the same principle
205	 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own `!recommendations?.recs?.length` gate already applies
206	 * (build plan step E1), just split into two named branches here because this page, unlike that
207	 * rail, has a real, visible empty-state component that must not flash for a shopper who does have
208	 * history.
209	 *
210	 * **Was gated on `recs.length` (the raw, pre-mapping Einstein count) until this fix** -- reasoned
211	 * at the time as avoiding a flash of the empty state while `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`
212	 * was still filtering what could turn out to be a fully-populated `recs` array. That reasoning
213	 * doesn't hold: `cards` (below) is a synchronous, same-render derivation of `recs` -- no separate
214	 * state, no separate effect -- so there is no such window to protect against, and gating on
215	 * `recs.length` instead left a real bug: when every rec fails to map (e.g. every product now
216	 * offline/deleted), `recs.length > 0` was still true, so the page took this branch and rendered
217	 * `<ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid cards={[]} />` -- which renders `null` per that component's own
218	 * documented contract for an empty `cards` array -- instead of falling through to
219	 * `EmptyRecentlyViewed`. A shopper with real (if all-stale) history saw a blank page with no
220	 * explanation. Gating on `cards.length` instead closes this without reintroducing any race, since
221	 * `isLoading` is still checked exactly as before.
222	 *
223	 * **First-paint window, inherited from `useEinstein()` itself, not new here:** `isLoading` and
224	 * `recommendations` both start at `false`/`[]` (`use-einstein.js:462-463`) on every render,
225	 * including the server-rendered one and this component's very first client render, before the
226	 * mount effect below has had any chance to run -- so, same as the pre-revision hook-based design
227	 * this replaces (that hook's own `useState` initial values were equally empty on first render),
228	 * there is a real window on first paint where this gate reads "not loading, zero recs" and renders
229	 * `EmptyRecentlyViewed`, until the effect fires and flips `isLoading` to `true`. Unlike the
230	 * pre-revision design, that fix-up was a synchronous `Storage` read (imperceptible); this one is a
231	 * real network round-trip (`getRecommendations` -> Einstein -> `getProducts` hydration), so the
232	 * window is not instant -- named here rather than left as a silent, undocumented regression. This
233	 * is a property of `useEinstein()`'s own initial state, not something this container introduces or
234	 * can resolve without changing that base SFCC hook (out of scope for this step).
235	 *
236	 * **SEO -- `noindex, nofollow`, via `Seo`'s `children`, not its `noIndex` prop.** Base `Seo`
237	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx:20`) emits
238	 * `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` for `noIndex` -- `noindex` only, never `nofollow`.
239	 * Passing both `noIndex` and an explicit `<meta name="robots">` child would emit two competing
240	 * `robots` tags, so `noIndex` is left unset and the full directive is passed as a child instead
241	 * (Marcel's explicit decision, build plan §B2). `<Seo>` is otherwise mounted exactly as
242	 * `home/index.tsx` mounts it -- `title`/`description` only, no extra props.
243	 *
244	 * `getTemplateName` matches the convention already used by every other page-level override
245	 * (`home`, `product-detail`, `product-list`, `experience`, `contentful-preview` -- see each file's
246	 * own `<Page>.getTemplateName = () => '<name>';` line, placed the same way here).
247	 */
248	const RecentlyViewed = () => {
249	  const intl = useIntl();
250	  const { isRegistered } = useCustomerType();
251	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getRecommendations } = useEinstein();
252	  const toast = useToast();
253	  const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
254	  // Site/locale prefixer for selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard's own `href` — see this file's
255	  // own module docblock for the fix this closes (2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, confirmed).
256	  const { buildUrl } = useMultiSite();
257	
258	  // Fires once on mount -- matches recommended-products/index.tsx's own Recently-Viewed branch
259	  // (build plan step E1), which fires the identical call for the identical recommender, just from
260	  // an effect with a wider dependency array (that component also handles other recommenders/zones
261	  // sharing one effect). This page only ever renders this one recommender, so an empty dependency
262	  // array is the direct equivalent -- `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is off repo-wide
263	  // (@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint/partials/react.js:26), and this exact
264	  // fire-once-on-mount-with-no-deps pattern already has a precedent needing no lint suppression:
265	  // home/index.tsx's own `useEffect(() => { einstein.sendViewPage(pathname); }, []);`.
266	  useEffect(() => {
267	    getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED);
268	  }, []);
269	
270	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's and recommended-products/index.tsx's own
271	  // consumers already use: formatPrice is injected into the mapper rather than formatted inside
272	  // it, keeping that mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
273	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string): string =>
274	    intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
275	
276	  // Size-aware Add to Bag (2026-09-09 full-parity-with-PLP build) -- keyed by product id rather
277	  // than product-list/index.tsx's own per-card `ProductListCard` wrapper with local `useState`:
278	  // that pattern needs a per-card component instance to own its own state, but this page's grid
279	  // (`ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) is a shared, already-shipped organism that renders `cards` directly
280	  // with no per-card wrapper slot of its own (unlike PLP, which builds its own grid inline with
281	  // full control) -- touching that organism's contract to add one would be a bigger, cross-cutting
282	  // change than this fix calls for (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5: never refactor upward). A single
283	  // id-keyed map at this container achieves the same "each card remembers its own selected size"
284	  // result without touching the Grid at all.
285	  const [selectedSizeChipValues, setSelectedSizeChipValues] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({});
286	
287	  const handleResolvedAddToBag = (orderableProductId: string, price: number | undefined) => {
288	    addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{ productId: orderableProductId, price, quantity: 1 }])
289	      .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))
290	      .catch(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE), status: 'error' }));
291	  };
292	
293	  // Normalized to a real array so every `recs.length`/`recs.map` reference below is safe without
294	  // repeating the optional chain at each call site -- `useEinstein()`'s own `recommendations`
295	  // state starts as a plain `[]` (use-einstein.js:463), which has no `.recs` property at all, so
296	  // `recommendations?.recs` reads `undefined` until the request above resolves.
297	  const recs: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct[] = recommendations?.recs ?? [];
298	
299	  const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recs
300	    .map((product): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
301	      const card = selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl);
302	      if (!card) return null;
303	
304	      const selectedSizeChipValue = selectedSizeChipValues[product.id];
305	      return {
306	        ...card,
307	        selectedSizeChipValue,
308	        onSizeChipSelect: (value: string) =>
309	          setSelectedSizeChipValues((previous) => ({ ...previous, [product.id]: value })),
310	        onAddToBag: () => {
311	          // No selection -> default-variant behaviour (matches product-list/index.tsx's own
312	          // ProductListCard.handleAddToBag exactly): no size selected means default size. A
313	          // selection that somehow matches no real variant falls back the same way, rather than
314	          // blocking the add entirely on a data mismatch.
315	          const resolved = selectedSizeChipValue ? resolveOrderableVariant(product, selectedSizeChipValue) : null;
316	          handleResolvedAddToBag(resolved?.productId ?? product.id, resolved?.price ?? product.price);
317	        },
318	      };
319	    })
320	    .filter((card): card is RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard => card !== null);
321	
322	  const title = intl.formatMessage(messages.title);
323	
324	  return (
325	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">
326	      <Seo title={title} description={PAGE_DESCRIPTION}>
327	        <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
328	      </Seo>
329	      {/* Screen-reader-only page heading — 2026-09-10, closing a real gap: this page had no
330	       * Heading element at all in either branch below, breaking the pattern product-list/index.tsx
331	       * and product-detail/index.tsx both already follow, and leaving however many real <h3>
332	       * product-name headings ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid renders (uncapped as of build plan step E4 --
333	       * see that component's own `cards` JSDoc) with nothing above them in the heading hierarchy
334	       * (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.3.1/2.4.6). `srOnly`,
335	       * matching product-detail/index.tsx's own <h1> exactly — the page's own visible title
336	       * styling (ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid's own textStyle="heading3" span, unchanged here) is a
337	       * separate, wider pre-existing pattern (several other organisms do the same thing) and out
338	       * of scope for this fix. */}
339	      <Heading as="h1" srOnly>
340	        {title}
341	      </Heading>
342	      {cards.length > 0 ? (
343	        // Bleeds the grid edge-to-edge past #app-main's own sitewide padding, matching the
344	        // Recently Viewed Rail's own flush treatment (product-detail/product-list's
345	        // <RecommendedProducts mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}>) — confirmed against this page's own
346	        // three real Figma frames (9551:78221 Desktop / 9560:137688 Tablet / 9560:138459 Mobile,
347	        // Zimmermann_Designs file), which show the header and every Product Card Group spanning
348	        // the full frame width, not inset within a page margin. ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid itself has
349	        // no passthrough/mx slot (unlike RecommendedProducts, which forwards `{...props}` to its
350	        // own wrapping Box for exactly this reason), so the bleed is applied here at the page
351	        // level instead. EmptyRecentlyViewed below is a distinct, centred layout with no
352	        // edge-to-edge requirement of its own — deliberately not wrapped the same way.
353	        //
354	        // APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — corrected 2026-09-10 (real, live-confirmed
355	        // bug: this page rendered wider than the viewport at every breakpoint, e.g. 1504px at a
356	        // 1440px Desktop viewport). This page has no PageContainer/layerStyle="page" second
357	        // containment layer the way PDP/PLP do — #app-main's own padding is the only thing here to
358	        // cancel — so it needs the single-layer constant, not the two-layer one. See that
359	        // constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the full root-cause math.
360	        <Box
361	          mx={APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX}
362	          // Space before the global Footer — Figma's own page frames (see the mx comment above
363	          // for the node ids) show this filled by "Footer Primary" (node 9560:110769 on Desktop,
364	          // same shape on Tablet/Mobile — a "Load More" button, deferred: real, Figma-annotated
365	          // functional requirement, not built yet, Marcel 2026-09-10), uniformly 32px top-padding +
366	          // 52px button + 80px bottom-padding = 164px on all three breakpoints, sitting flush
367	          // against both the last card row above it and the real Footer below it (zero extra gap
368	          // either side, confirmed directly). With no button to render, only the padding portion
369	          // is reserved here (32+80=112px, Marcel's own call, 2026-09-10) — not the button's own
370	          // 52px, since there's nothing occupying that height right now. This will need to grow by
371	          // that 52px once Load More is actually built; that future component replaces this
372	          // padding entirely rather than sitting alongside it.
373	          paddingBottom="calc(var(--zimm-scale-800) + var(--zimm-scale-5xl))" // 32px + 80px = 112px
374	        >
375	          <ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid
376	            title={title}
377	            itemCountLabel={intl.formatMessage(messages.itemCount, { count: cards.length })}
378	            cards={cards}
379	          />
380	        </Box>
381	      ) : !isLoading && cards.length === 0 ? (
382	        <EmptyRecentlyViewed isRegistered={isRegistered} />
383	      ) : null}
384	    </Box>
385	  );
386	};
387	
388	RecentlyViewed.getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed';
389

1	import React from 'react';
2	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
3	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import { useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount } from 'app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount';
6	import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
7	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation } from '../zimmProductCard';
8	
9	/**
10	 * The narrow `recentlyViewed`-only slice of the full `ZimmProductCardProps` union — this
11	 * component only ever renders that one variation (see this file's own module docblock), so
12	 * `cards` below is typed against exactly that, not the full four-variation union (narrowed
13	 * 2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, confirmed: the wider union let a caller pass e.g. a
14	 * `plp`-shaped card with no compile error, even though nothing here would ever render its
15	 * `plp`-only fields). Both halves are real, already-exported types from `zimmProductCard` —
16	 * see that module's own `ZimmProductCardBaseProps`/`ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation`.
17	 */
18	export type ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation;
19	
20	// Same `chakra(RouteLink)` wrap this component family already establishes for its own internal
21	// links (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's `MediaOnlyCardLink`, zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx's
22	// `ProductNameLink`) — used here for the See-Full-History link, which navigates to the SFCC-84
23	// Recently Viewed Full History page, an internal route, not an external URL.
24	const SeeAllLink = chakra(RouteLink);
25	
26	export type ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps = {
27	  /**
28	   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl (the container, A6,
29	   * does). **Styling resolved 2026-09-08** (was previously left unstyled pending confirmation —
30	   * live Storybook testing caught the resulting bug: the title rendered in the ambient body
31	   * weight, Futura Round 400, instead of the design's intended weight): this component now
32	   * applies `textStyle="heading3"` itself when rendering `title`, matching the exact spec
33	   * confirmed against the Full History page's own title bar this same session (Figma
34	   * `Default/h3-strong` — Futura Round, 16px/18 line-height, weight 500, letter-spacing -0.12px,
35	   * uppercase — cross-checked against this codebase's registered `heading3` token, an exact
36	   * match). Applying it here rather than requiring every caller to pre-style the title guarantees
37	   * the design intent regardless of what a caller passes; a caller supplying an already fully
38	   * styled element can still override any of this via its own more-specific styling.
39	   */
40	  title: ReactNode;
41	  /**
42	   * Rendered in the exact order received (AC 2: most-recent-first, left to right) — no sorting or
43	   * reordering happens here. Capped to `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS` for the current real
44	   * breakpoint regardless of length — a hard cap, not a "fits before scrolling" soft limit (see
45	   * that constant's own comment, app/constants/index.ts, and this component's own render-body
46	   * comment below for why the cap has to live here rather than in the request that produced this
47	   * array).
48	   */
49	  cards: readonly ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps[];
50	  /** Href to the SFCC-84 Recently Viewed Full History page. The See-Full-History link only
51	   *  renders when this is provided — see the render body below. */
52	  seeAllHref?: string;
53	  /**
54	   * No default/fallback text is supplied when this is omitted while `seeAllHref` is provided —
55	   * this component owns no copy or intl (see the module docblock), so inventing an English
56	   * fallback here would risk shipping untranslated text on non-English storefronts. In real usage
57	   * the container (A6) is expected to always supply this alongside `seeAllHref`.
58	   */
59	  seeAllLabel?: string;
60	};
61	
62	const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedRail';
63	
64	/**
65	 * SFCC-83 — the Recently Viewed rail organism (build plan section A5). Purely presentational:
66	 * data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — see
67	 * .claude/rules/components.md's container/presentational split. The container (A6) is
68	 * responsible for building `cards` (via A3's Einstein-rec-to-card mapper), gating this
69	 * component's visibility (A4's `hasRecentlyViewed`), and supplying `title`/`seeAllLabel` copy.
70	 *
71	 * Structure mirrors Figma exactly: a `header` row (title left, the See-Full-History link right)
72	 * above a `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s. No rail-level arrow buttons — `ZimmProductCardMedia`
73	 * already carries its own intra-card carousel arrows, and a second set at the rail level would
74	 * collide with them (see zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own docblock for the Figma node
75	 * evidence).
76	 *
77	 * **`group`'s horizontal scroll/scroll-snap (zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts) is a narrow-viewport
78	 * safety net, not the "more cards exist, scroll to see them" mechanism it might look like.**
79	 * Confirmed with Marcel (2026-09-08): the per-breakpoint card count below is a hard cap — a
80	 * shopper on a real, design-reference-width device never has more cards to scroll to than the
81	 * cap allows; "more history exists" is surfaced via the See-Full-History link (the container's
82	 * own job), not via scrolling this rail further. The scroll/scroll-snap CSS stays
83	 * meaningful only for a real device narrower than the design reference itself (e.g. a phone
84	 * under ~402px), where the capped card count can still slightly overflow the actual viewport.
85	 *
86	 * `cards` is typed as `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps` (`ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
87	 * ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation`, declared above) — not the full `ZimmProductCardProps`
88	 * union this step's own given component contract originally specified verbatim (narrowed
89	 * 2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, confirmed: this component only ever renders the
90	 * `recentlyViewed` variation, so the wider union let a caller pass e.g. a `plp`-shaped card with
91	 * no compile error, even though nothing here would ever render its `plp`-only fields). This
92	 * component therefore still spreads each entry straight into `ZimmProductCard`
93	 * (`<ZimmProductCard {...card} />`) rather than forcing `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` onto every
94	 * card itself — every entry already carries that variation by construction (A3's mapper produces
95	 * `recentlyViewed`-shaped cards) and now by the type itself, since `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps`
96	 * has no other variation to be. Type-only change: `ZimmProductCard`'s own prop type is still the
97	 * full union, and a `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps` value is one real member of it, so this compiles
98	 * and renders identically to before.
99	 *
100	 * `data-testid="product-card"` / `data-product-id` on each rendered card come from
101	 * `ZimmProductCard`'s own root (zimmProductCard/index.tsx: "a DOM hook for QA automation/
102	 * analytics") — this component adds no additional per-card test hook of its own.
103	 */
104	export const ZimmRecentlyViewedRail = ({ title, cards, seeAllHref, seeAllLabel }: ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps) => {
105	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_RECIPE, {});
106	
107	  // Cap is enforced here, client-side, regardless of how many cards were passed in — the data
108	  // source (Einstein's own `recommendations.recs`, wired in build plan step E1) does not itself
109	  // honour a requested limit, and per-breakpoint capping is this component's own presentational
110	  // concern, not the container's. Falls back to the smallest (base/mobile) count on the very first render
111	  // before the client-side media-query match resolves (see RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS's
112	  // own comment, app/constants/index.ts, for why this is a hard per-breakpoint cap, not a "fits
113	  // before scrolling" soft limit). A slice, never a sort — order is otherwise untouched (AC 2).
114	  //
115	  // `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount()`, not a direct `useBreakpointValue` call (corrected
116	  // 2026-09-10 — see that hook's own docblock for the live-confirmed bug this closes): this
117	  // component's own Desktop card-width styling (zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's
118	  // `DESKTOP_UP_QUERY`) switches at 1024px, not this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px) that
119	  // `useBreakpointValue` would have resolved against — the two disagreeing meant a real, narrow
120	  // window (1024–1280px) where cards were already styled for 5 slots but only 3 were allowed to
121	  // render.
122	  const maxVisibleCards = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
123	  const visibleCards = cards.slice(0, maxVisibleCards);
124	
125	  // Second guard behind A4's own visibility gate, which lives in the container, not here — an
126	  // empty rail renders nothing at all, not an empty shell.
127	  if (visibleCards.length === 0) {
128	    return null;
129	  }
130	
131	  return (
132	    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-rail">
133	      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
134	        {/* flex/minWidth match Figma's own title node (flex: 1 0 0, min-w-px) — grows to fill
135	            whatever `header`'s own gap + the link's width don't claim, and can shrink below its
136	            own text's intrinsic width rather than force an overflow. See zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's
137	            own "TITLE/LINK SPACING" docblock section. */}
138	        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" flex="1 0 0" minWidth={0}>
139	          {title}
140	        </chakra.span>
141	        {seeAllHref && seeAllLabel && (
142	          <SeeAllLink to={seeAllHref} textStyle="linkLg" __css={styles.seeAllLink}>
143	            {seeAllLabel}
144	          </SeeAllLink>
145	        )}
146	      </chakra.div>
147	      <chakra.div __css={styles.group} data-testid="recently-viewed-rail-group">
148	        {visibleCards.map((card) => (
149	          <chakra.div key={card.id} __css={styles.card}>
150	            <ZimmProductCard {...card} />
151	          </chakra.div>
152	        ))}
153	      </chakra.div>
154	    </chakra.div>
155	  );
156	};

196	 * `badge` field is always `undefined` -- the plain `getProducts` endpoint this build reads from has
197	 * no confirmed `c_productBadges` field (see that mapper's own docblock's "Badge" section). A card
198	 * rendered by this page will never show a badge yet; this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap for
199	 * this step, not a bug in this file.
200	 *
201	 * **Empty-state gate (build plan step E2, decision #3; corrected 2026-09-15 -- CodeRabbit finding,
202	 * personally verified before treating as valid):** `cards.length > 0` renders the grid;
203	 * `!isLoading && cards.length === 0` renders `EmptyRecentlyViewed`; anything else (i.e. `isLoading`
204	 * still `true`, request in flight) renders neither -- the same principle
205	 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own `!recommendations?.recs?.length` gate already applies
206	 * (build plan step E1), just split into two named branches here because this page, unlike that
207	 * rail, has a real, visible empty-state component that must not flash for a shopper who does have
208	 * history.
209	 *
210	 * **Was gated on `recs.length` (the raw, pre-mapping Einstein count) until this fix** -- reasoned
211	 * at the time as avoiding a flash of the empty state while `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`
212	 * was still filtering what could turn out to be a fully-populated `recs` array. That reasoning
213	 * doesn't hold: `cards` (below) is a synchronous, same-render derivation of `recs` -- no separate
214	 * state, no separate effect -- so there is no such window to protect against, and gating on
215	 * `recs.length` instead left a real bug: when every rec fails to map (e.g. every product now
216	 * offline/deleted), `recs.length > 0` was still true, so the page took this branch and rendered
217	 * `<ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid cards={[]} />` -- which renders `null` per that component's own
218	 * documented contract for an empty `cards` array -- instead of falling through to
219	 * `EmptyRecentlyViewed`. A shopper with real (if all-stale) history saw a blank page with no
220	 * explanation. Gating on `cards.length` instead closes this without reintroducing any race, since
221	 * `isLoading` is still checked exactly as before.
222	 *

309	    if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
310	      // PostBuild fix round, Fix 1 (2026-09-15): Recently-Viewed only, report just the recs that
311	      // actually survived `selectRecentlyViewedCard`'s own null-filtering below — the same set the
312	      // render branch further down turns into `cards` — not the full raw `recommendations.recs`.
313	      // Every other recommender has no filtering step at all between its raw recs and what
314	      // actually renders, so the `else` branch below is the exact original, unchanged expression —
315	      // this `ids` computation changes nothing for them.
316	      //
317	      // Without this, a Recently-Viewed rec that fails to map (e.g. no usable name/image — see
318	      // that mapper's own hard-gate contract) still got reported to Einstein/DataCloud as
319	      // "viewed" even though the rail never actually rendered it: if every one of a shopper's
320	      // recently-viewed products failed to map, the rail correctly rendered nothing, but this
321	      // effect still told Einstein/DataCloud the shopper viewed every one of them — false signal
322	      // into Einstein's own recommendation-quality feedback loop, and silent (nothing on screen
323	      // indicated it happened).
324	      //
325	      // Recomputing `selectRecentlyViewedCard` here rather than sharing the render branch's own
326	      // `cards` (declared later in this same function, out of this effect's reach) is an accepted,
327	      // cheap duplicate — this effect only ever fires once per mount, since `isOnScreen` is itself
328	      // `useOnce: true` (use-intersection-observer.js). `recommender`/`formatPrice`/`buildUrl` are
329	      // read here without being added to the dependency array below, matching this same effect's
330	      // pre-existing omission of `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud` — `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is off
331	      // repo-wide (see recentlyViewed/index.tsx's own docblock for the exact config line), and
332	      // `formatPrice`/`buildUrl` are recreated every render, so adding them would make this effect
333	      // re-fire on every render instead of once per mount.
334	      const ids: { id?: string }[] =
335	        recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED
336	          ? recommendations.recs
337	              .map((product: RecentlyViewedProduct) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl))
338	              .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
339	              .map((card: RecentlyViewedCard) => ({ id: card.id }))
340	          : recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id }));
341	
342	      // Recently-Viewed only: nothing survived the mapping above, so nothing actually rendered —
343	      // report no impression at all, rather than an empty-but-still-sent call. Gated on the
344	      // recommender check too, not just `ids.length`, so the other four recommenders keep firing
345	      // unconditionally exactly as before, even in the (untouched, pre-existing) case where their
346	      // own raw `recs` happens to be an empty array.
347	      if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED && ids.length === 0) {
348	        return;
349	      }
350	
351	      sendViewReco(
352	        {
353	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
354	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,

       dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations(

-        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),

content.text:
All five fixes are implemented, verified, and scoped exactly to the four named files — nothing else was touched.

## Fix 1 — impression-tracking now only reports what actually rendered

**Consequence:** if every one of a shopper's recently-viewed products failed to map to a card (e.g. all now offline/deleted), the rail correctly showed nothing, but Einstein/DataCloud were still told the shopper "viewed" all of them. False signal into Einstein's own recommendation-quality loop, invisible on screen.

**Mechanism:** the impression effect (`overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`) ran before the Recently-Viewed branch's own `selectRecentlyViewedCard` null-filtering, so it read the raw `recommendations.recs` instead of the filtered set the render path calls `cards`.

**Fix — before:**
```tsx
sendViewReco({...}, recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })));
dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations({...}, recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })));
```
**After:**
```tsx
const ids: { id?: string }[] =
  recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED
    ? recommendations.recs
        .map((product: RecentlyViewedProduct) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl))
        .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
        .map((card: RecentlyViewedCard) => ({ id: card.id }))
    : recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id }));

if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED && ids.length === 0) {
  return; // nothing rendered, nothing to report
}
sendViewReco({...}, ids);
dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations({...}, ids);
```
The `else` branch is byte-identical to the original expression — a non-RV recommender never enters the `recommender === PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch, so nothing changes for it.

**Other-4-recommenders verification, not assumed:** no test in this file exercised this effect at all before today — `isOnScreen` was globally stubbed to always `false`, so `if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs)` never ran its body in any existing test. I made the stub overridable per-test (`vi.hoisted`) and added a new test using `PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE` that asserts `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` fire with the full raw `[{id:'other-1'},{id:'other-2'}]` list, proving the `else` path fires unconditionally exactly as before. This one test generalises to the other 3 recommenders because the branch is keyed only on `recommender === PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` — nothing else differs per recommender name — but I did not run one test per name; flagging that rather than overclaiming.

**Prove-don't-assert, actually done, not just narrated:** I temporarily reverted the effect to its pre-fix form, ran only the new Fix-1 test — it failed for exactly the claimed reason (`mockSendViewReco` called once with `rec-1`/`rec-2`, both of which fail mapping) — then restored the fix and re-ran; it passed.

## Fix 2 — corrected the docblock's false "same principle" claim

Target was `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (the task said "same file" but literally described "the page's `cards.length`-based gate" and quoted "the same principle" — that exact phrase only exists in this file, confirmed via grep; the "recentlyViewed/index.tsx" name in the task text is the accurate pointer). Replaced the claim that the page's gate works "the same" as the rail's raw-count gate with the real reason they differ: the rail's `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` has its own downstream `visibleCards.length === 0 → null` guard so a raw-count mismatch is harmless there, but this page has no such guard and a real three-way outcome (grid vs. friendly empty-state vs. loading) to get right — plus a pointer to Fix 1 as the place impression-tracking parity actually mattered.

## Fix 3 — new test proving Fix 1

`overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx`: made the `use-intersection-observer` and `use-datacloud` mocks stable/overridable (via `vi.hoisted`, matching the existing precedent at `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx:17-19`), then added two tests — the RV all-fail-to-map case (asserts no impression at all) and the other-recommender confirming case (asserts the full raw list still reports). Both pass; the revert-and-confirm-fail cycle above is the required proof step.

## Fix 4 — two stale comments in `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`

Both (module docblock line ~69, render-guard comment line ~125) previously described the deleted `useRecentlyViewedHistory` hook's `hasRecentlyViewed` as the current visibility gate. Corrected to state the real, current gate: the container's `!recommendations?.recs?.length` check in `recommended-products/index.tsx` (build plan step E1); this component has never gated its own visibility beyond `visibleCards.length === 0`. Comment-only, confirmed via diff — no code lines touched.

## Fix 5 — spelling

`overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`: `Normalized` → `Normalised`. One word, confirmed the only instance.

## Evidence

```
npx tsc --noEmit          → clean, no output, exit 0
npm run test -- --run     → 85 files passed, 1310 tests passed, 0 failed
```
`recipeGuards.test.ts` (the styling gate) passed — expected, since nothing styling-related changed. Re-ran the three directly-touched test files individually as a second confirmation: 28/28 passed (`recommended-products/index.test.tsx`, `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx`, `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.test.tsx`).

`git status --porcelain` shows exactly the four named files touched, nothing else:
`overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`.

## Unverified gaps

- I did not test this against a real Einstein/DataCloud endpoint (Einstein remains "Not Deployed" per project memory — this was already untestable in a live sense before this fix too).
- I did not run `npm run lint` or a CodeRabbit review — this invocation's stated done-criteria were `tsc` + `test` only, and there's no commit/PR for CodeRabbit to review against; scaling to what was asked rather than adding machinery.
- I verified the "other 4 recommenders unaffected" claim via one representative recommender (`PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE`) plus code-path reasoning (the branch is keyed only on the RV recommender string, nothing else differs per name) — not one test per literal recommender name.

## What Marcel is missing

Nothing new bug-wise, but one thing worth knowing: `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` and `PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` resolve to the identical string (already documented elsewhere in this file), so Fix 1's `recommender === PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch technically also matches when Cart passes its own recommender value — harmless today only because Cart's render branch returns `null` before ever attaching `ref`, so `isOnScreen` never goes true there. That's pre-existing, not something this fix changes, but it's a second place (beyond the render logic) where "Cart and PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED are indistinguishable by value" is silently relied on rather than checked — worth a real `isCartPage` guard inside the effect itself if this file ever grows a case where Cart's ref *could* attach.
